I will keep most of my land in the wheat-maize rotation and leave a smaller part for cotton. I am 65, and some people in my family work off-farm, so I will not push too much labor-heavy cotton. With well irrigation and my years of experience, I trust wheat and maize more for steady grain and easier field management. I will put 6 mu into winter wheat, and after harvest I will plant summer maize on that same 6 mu. I will keep 3 mu for cotton because I still know that crop well and it brings cash, but I will not expand it. For wheat, I will use improved seed, apply enough nitrogen first and then topdress once, with moderate phosphorus and potassium, irrigate about three times, and spray a couple of times if disease or insects show up. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because it gives better yield, keep fertilizer balanced but focus on nitrogen, use one or two irrigations depending on rain, and do lighter pesticide use. For cotton, I will use hybrid seed, give it steady fertilizer and more potassium than grain crops, irrigate several times because I have a well, and spray more often because cotton usually needs closer insect control. I will choose tillage that saves labor where possible, especially after wheat, because I want work that I can still manage steadily this year.
